elements.char: Introduction
elements.label: text

elements.char: Proteins, including the globular, fibrous, membrane and intrinsically disordered proteins, are
elements.label: text

elements.char: responsible for diverse functions in almost every process of cellular life. Globular proteins, as
elements.label: text

elements.char: the majority type of the proteins in nature, can fold from disordered peptide chains into spe-
elements.label: text

elements.char: cific three-dimensional (3D) structures on minimal-frustrated energy landscape [1–4]. Such
elements.label: text

elements.char: kind of 3D structures, which are encoded by the amino acid sequences, are known as native
elements.label: text

elements.char: states. It is worth noting that the native state of a protein is not static, but exhibits dynamical
elements.label: text

elements.char: fluctuations around the energy minimum. Experiments and molecular simulations have
elements.label: text

elements.char: shown that thermal fluctuations trigger the motions of proteins such as domain movements
elements.label: text

elements.char: and allosteric transitions, which enable the biological functions of proteins such as catalysis
elements.label: text

elements.char: [5], ligand binding [6, 7], biomolecular recognition [8], and transportation [9]. Uncovering
elements.label: text

elements.char: the relations between the structure and the function of proteins is a fundamental question in
elements.label: text

elements.char: molecular biophysics. To answer it, the fluctuations at the native states may provide a key.
elements.label: text

elements.char: One of the most fascinating properties of proteins is the long-range correlated fluctuations
elements.label: text

elements.char: around the native states [10–12]. Thanks to the long-range correlations, local perturbations to
elements.label: text

elements.char: any residue can be sensed by every other residue of the entire protein, even when the two sites
elements.label: text

elements.char: are spatially distant. Such a property plays an important role in the functionality of the pro-
elements.label: text

elements.char: teins. For example, for allosteric proteins, long-range correlations warrant the binding at one
elements.label: text

elements.char: site can be transmitted to other functional sites [13, 14], and enable the high susceptibility for
elements.label: text

elements.char: proteins in cellular environments. Based on the correlation analysis of structural ensembles
elements.label: text

elements.char: determined by solution nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), it was already demonstrated
elements.label: text

elements.char: that the native proteins exhibit long-range correlations and high susceptibility in the native
elements.label: text

elements.char: dynamics [15]. Such a phenomenon is also in line with other theoretical and experimental
elements.label: text

elements.char: results, for example, the long-range conformational forces related to the hydrophobicity scales
elements.label: text

elements.char: of the proteins [16–20], the fractal dimension in the oscillation spectrum [21] and configura-
elements.label: text

elements.char: tion space [22], the slow relaxation of protein molecules in the solution [23, 24], the volume
elements.label: text

elements.char: fluctuation of allosteric proteins [25], and the overlap between the low-frequency collective
elements.label: text

elements.char: oscillation modes and large-scale conformational changes in allosteric transitions [26–30].
elements.label: text

elements.char: Accumulating evidence indicates that native proteins are not only stable enough to warrant
elements.label: text

elements.char: structural robustness, but also susceptible enough to sense the signals in the milieu, and ready
elements.label: text

elements.char: to perform large-scale conformational changes. However, the origin of such kind of dynamics
elements.label: text

elements.char: is still unclear.
elements.label: text

elements.char: In the present paper, we concentrate on the structure and the equilibrium fluctuation
elements.label: text

elements.char: dynamics of a large set of globular proteins determined by X-ray crystallography, ranging
elements.label: text

elements.char: from a single hairpin structure to large protein assemblies. Firstly, to elucidate the connection
elements.label: text

elements.char: between the long-range correlations and protein structures, we conduct correlation analysis
elements.label: text

elements.char: based on the elastic network models (ENMs) [26–30]. We find that the long-range correlations
elements.label: text

elements.char: and the scaling laws can be robustly reproduced by the ENMs with different model parameters.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Such a result indicates that the long-range correlations are encoded in the native topology of
elements.label: text

elements.char: the proteins. Secondly, we conduct normal mode analysis [31–33] for protein molecules, ideal
elements.label: text

elements.char: polymer chains, and lattice systems. A similar scaling relation holds for polymers, lattices, and
elements.label: text

elements.char: proteins, but the scaling coefficients are different. Such a result shows how native proteins bal-
elements.label: text

elements.char: ance between order and disorder, which resemble the physical systems near the critical point
elements.label: text

elements.char: of a phase transition. Thirdly, we introduce the average path length and modularity to describe
elements.label: text

elements.char: the topological characteristics of the proteins. Scaling relations are also observed between these
elements.label: text

elements.char: topological descriptors and the size of the proteins. According to the result of the scaling analy-
elements.label: text

elements.char: sis, we conclude that native proteins show both dense packing and fractal topology. Lastly, we
elements.label: text
